title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Trial of Maritime Freight Forwarding Dispute Cases

articles.content_en: Article 2 When a People's Court tries a case involving a maritime freight forwarding dispute, if it determines that a freight forwarding enterprise and a principal have formed different legal relationships such as agency, transport, or warehousing due to the handling of maritime freight forwarding affairs, it shall apply the relevant legal provisions respectively.

Article 3 A People's Court shall determine whether a maritime freight forwarding contract relationship is established according to the nature of the rights and obligations agreed in the written contract, taking into comprehensive consideration the name and method by which the freight forwarding enterprise obtains remuneration, the types of invoices issued and charging items, the transaction practices between the parties, and other circumstances of actual performance of the contract.

Article 4 Where a freight forwarding enterprise issues a bill of lading, sea waybill, or other transport document in its own name in the course of handling maritime freight forwarding affairs, and the principal claims on that basis that the freight forwarding enterprise shall bear carrier liability, the People's Court shall support it.
Where a freight forwarding enterprise issues a bill of lading, sea waybill, or other transport document in the name of an agent of the carrier, but cannot prove that it has obtained authorization from the carrier, and the principal claims on that basis that the freight forwarding enterprise shall bear carrier liability, the People's Court shall support it.

Article 5 Where the principal and the freight forwarding enterprise have agreed on the authority for sub-entrustment, and a party claims that the principal consented to the sub-entrustment with respect to maritime freight forwarding affairs within the scope of authority, the People's Court shall support it.
Where there is no agreement on the authority for sub-entrustment, and the freight forwarding enterprise or a third party claims that the principal consented to the sub-entrustment on the ground that the principal knew that the freight forwarding enterprise had sub-entrusted or partially sub-entrusted the maritime freight forwarding affairs to a third party and did not express opposition, the People's Court shall not support it, except where the principal's conduct clearly indicates that the principal accepted the sub-entrustment.

Article 6 Where a party has reason to believe that an actor has the authority to represent the other party in concluding a maritime freight forwarding contract on the basis of the transaction practices between the parties, and that party claims that the contract is established pursuant to Article 172 of the Civil Code, the People's Court shall support it.

Article 7 Where a maritime freight forwarding contract stipulates that the delivery by the freight forwarding enterprise of documents obtained from handling maritime freight forwarding affairs is conditional on the principal's payment of relevant fees, and the freight forwarding enterprise refuses to deliver the documents on the ground that the principal has not paid the relevant fees, the People's Court shall support it.
Where the contract has no stipulation or the stipulation is unclear, and the freight forwarding enterprise refuses to deliver the documents on the ground that the principal has not paid the relevant fees, the People's Court shall support it, except for bills of lading, sea waybills, or other transport documents.

Article 8 Where a freight forwarding enterprise accepts the entrustment of a contractual shipper to handle booking affairs, and at the same time accepts the entrustment of an actual shipper to deliver goods to a carrier, and the actual shipper requests the freight forwarding enterprise to deliver the bill of lading, sea waybill, or other transport document obtained by it, the People's Court shall support it.
A contractual shipper means a person who concludes a contract for the carriage of goods by sea with a carrier by himself, or entrusts another person to do so in his name, or entrusts another person to do so for his benefit.
An actual shipper means a person who delivers goods to the carrier related to the contract for the carriage of goods by sea by himself, or entrusts another person to do so in his name, or entrusts another person to do so for his benefit.

Article 9 Where a freight forwarding enterprise completes maritime freight forwarding affairs in accordance with the authority of general entrustment and requests the principal to pay relevant reasonable expenses, the People's Court shall support it.

Article 10 Where a principal claims that a freight forwarding enterprise shall bear corresponding compensation liability on the ground that the freight forwarding enterprise caused losses to the principal in handling maritime freight forwarding affairs, the People's Court shall support it, unless the freight forwarding enterprise proves that it is not at fault.

Article 11 Where a freight forwarding enterprise fails to exercise due care and concludes a contract for the carriage of goods by sea with an operator of non-vessel operating common carrier service that has not registered its bills of lading with the competent transportation department of China, thereby causing losses to the principal, it shall bear corresponding compensation liability.

Article 12 Where a freight forwarding enterprise accepts the entrustment of an operator of non-vessel operating common carrier service that has not registered its bills of lading with the competent transportation department of China to issue bills of lading, and a party claims that the freight forwarding enterprise and the operator of non-vessel operating common carrier service shall bear joint and several liability for the losses under the bills of lading, the People's Court shall support it.
After bearing compensation liability, the freight forwarding enterprise shall have the right to seek recourse from the operator of non-vessel operating common carrier service.
Article 13 Lawsuits brought for the disputes listed in Article 1 of these Provisions shall be under the jurisdiction of maritime courts.

Article 14 Where, in the course of adjudicating a case, a People's Court discovers that a freight forwarding enterprise that does not have the qualification to engage in non-vessel operating common carrier business has, in violation of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on International Maritime Transportation, issued a bill of lading, sea waybill, or other transport document in its own name, it shall issue a judicial recommendation to the competent transportation department, recommending that the transportation department impose a penalty.
Article 15 These Provisions do not apply to freight forwarding dispute cases related to the carriage of goods along the coast or in inland rivers.

Article 16 Where judicial interpretations previously made by this Court before the coming into force of these Provisions conflict with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.
After these Provisions come into force, where a case is still in the first instance or second instance stage, these Provisions shall apply; where a case has already been finally adjudicated before these Provisions come into force, and where a party applies for retrial after these Provisions come into force or a case is decided to be retried in accordance with the trial supervision procedure, these Provisions shall not apply.
